newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on tight liquidity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed early falls to close higher against its U.S. counterpart on Monday amid tightening liquidity in the money market due to a red-hot bourse, dealers said.
The local unit ended at an intraday high T$27.892 against Saturday's T$27.902 close, reversing an early-trade low of T$27.919.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$214 million.
"Since liquidity becomes tight, many investors turn to sell U.S. dollars in exchange for Taiwan dollars," said one dealer.

At 0820 GMT, the overnight interbank rate was at 8.274 percent against Saturday's 7.782 close -- far outside the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent, as the recently red-hot stock market sucked funds out of the banking system.
The rejuvenated stock market sizzled anew on Monday to further a two-week-old bull run, ending 91.29 points or 1.03 percent higher at a seven-year closing high 8,925.12.

Dealers voiced caution about a further weakening, pointing to what they called clear signs of significant and well-timed central bank intervention late last week that prevented the recently easing Taiwan dollar from falling further.
Dealers said they saw no significant new foreign equity fund inflows even though the stock market had surged some 12 percent since late May to hit new seven-year high.

"Foreign funds did not take immediate moves because they probably were evaluating whether it would be risky or not to reenter the market, which had surged (some 12 percent) since late May," another dealer said.
A T$27.87-27.92 range was seen for Tuesday.
